claims.claim_text: The frozen literature identifies the Picard/Bianchi geodesic object and supports primitive-conjugacy and inversion vocabulary, but these object-level sources do not define a Gaussian-prime-ideal owner law.

negative_constraints.rule: Do not infer an owner map, an owner quotient, or S_H from object identity or primitive-geodesic terminology.

claims.claim_text: Arithmetic-Kleinian, arithmetic-group, three-manifold, word-hyperbolic, and integral-matrix algorithms are conditional components rather than a completed level-(3) primitive, conjugacy, inversion, and unoriented-owner quotient.

negative_constraints.rule: Do not equate adjacent algorithms with the exact level-(3) PSL_2(Z[i]) conjugacy relation without a proved reduction and complete certificate contract.

claims.claim_text: Computational ideal arithmetic, factorization, and ideal-power detection can support validation layers, but they neither select one literal Gaussian prime-ideal owner nor prove group-element primitivity.

negative_constraints.rule: Do not conflate ideal maximal-power detection with maximal roots of loxodromic group elements or with owner selection.

claims.claim_text: A literal owner mechanism must reconcile the unoriented inversion quotient with representative-independent selection of one member of a conjugate split-prime-ideal pair, and the closed corpus does not instantiate that law.

negative_constraints.rule: Do not weaken the codomain to a norm, rational prime, residue, composite ideal, or unordered conjugate pair.
Do not promote the closed-corpus gap into an impossibility or novelty claim.

claims.claim_text: Mechanism admissibility and primitive-owner quotient completeness are independent pre-performance kill gates; neither may be selected, repaired, or certified by finite collision-separation performance.

negative_constraints.rule: Do not report either gate as closed, and do not report a value of S_H.

negative_constraints.rule: Describe every prospective proof, registry, quotient, control, holdout, and computation as unexecuted and separately authorized.
